newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ average hourly earnings rise 3.3 pct in May yr.
newsitem.headline: NZ average hourly earnings rise 3.3 pct in May yr.

text.p: New Zealand average hourly earnings rose 3.3 percent to NZ$16.09 in the year to May 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
SNZ said this was the largest annual increase since August 1991.

After revisions, the rise in average hourly earnings for the year to February 1996 was 3.1 percent, down from a provisional 3.2 percent rise. The 3.3 percent rise in the May year is final, not provisional.
The average ordinary time hourly earnings of employees rose 3.4 percent in the May year, following rises of 3.0 percent and 3.2 percent in the November 1995 and February 1996 years.
In the public sector, average ordinary time hourly earnings rose 2.2 percent in the year, to $17.77, while in the private sector they rose 4.0 percent, to $15.36.
Female ordinary time hourly earnings, at NZ$14.08, were 80.6 percent of male earnings ($17.46), the lowest level since 1994.

Average overtime hourly earnings rose by 3.7 percent in the May year. SNZ said the May quarter was the 11th successive quarter in which an annual increase was recorded, after six successive decreases during 1992 and 1993.
Average total weekly earnings of full-time equivalent employees were 2.5 percent higher than a year ago, at $628.11.
